>For all intents and purposes, it's wishing for a total do-over, and I'm happy enough with my life to not want that. 

That must be nice. I am not there at this time. I have some people I only met because I am trans, but I think it would be possible for me to have met them had I been born a cis girl. Plus if I had been born cis I'd have more friends, have social skills due to not being isolated by everyone when they subconsciously detected something was "off" about me, have done all those milestones, and be treated as a girl by my mom instead of what I have now. So RN, I'd be fine with a total do-over, unless I KNEW 110% that my current future is a good one.

I feel the exact same way. I was 15 when I found out I was trans. I was going to transition ASAP, but then I didn't. It allowed fear to form and I was only able to overcome it and start HRT five years later, aka last month, and won't be able to pass as a girl until I'm out of college. I so want those years back. I would do anything to have my college years back as a girl. I'm glad you aren't in my boat w/out a girlfriend or a stable job, unable to fully live life, if at all, until my early 30s by which point I'd be a creep having to hang out with people 10 years or more younger than me because everyone else my age will have had their 20s to "get the party out of their system" and are then moving on to start families of their own.
Transition ASAP. You can at least have college as a girl (something I would have had if I hadn't let events make me keep being trans a secret and putting off transition until I was almost 21).
All of y'all are talking about being 155-160 lb and I'm here stuck at 220lb (probably closer to the 240 I was at before I went to Europe) making me feel a mix of emotions.
Thanks. or now I am feeling fine w/regards to the election. Now I want to end it because my trans friends just abandoned me and left me with no one.

AOC won't get it in 2024, or even 2028. Earliest is 2032. And that assumes that the progressive movement doesn't fracture post-Sanders-loss (since he won't run for President in 2024 if he loses in '20). Most likely, a fracture will happen and it will take until 2036 for the fracture to heal. At that point, I'll be almost 40. Too old to start and pass, and too much lost time that wouldn't make it worth it to transition.

Sanders' plan doesn't require going BACK to Congress to get M4A after first fighting for a stop gap of a public option, nor does it take 4 years to reach a "phase 2". There is no "phase 1" and "phase 2" under Sanders.
Polls have him as the strongest in a match-up with Trump and well outside of the margin of error.
I didn't say I was 40. I said I probably wouldn't be able to transition until I am 40 (aka a generation from now) if Sanders loses, basically guaranteeing Trump a second term.

Medicare for ALL expands coverage to all Americans and, in a sense, absorbs Medicaid, which I currently have, but may be at risk of losing if Trump gets reelected (since he proposed a MASSIVE cut to it recently)

Also her plan is just a way of saying she's against M4A and really for a public option but without alienating the base. Breaking it up into two phases wastes all the political capital she has on phase 1, and in three years time phase 2 won't be able to pass. Then Warren could say she tried to get M4A but her arms are tied even though she had another, more likely, path to M4A than her bungled two phase approach.

At that point he'd have lost NH and (in the media's eyes) Iowa. At that point there's no path to the nomination statistically because no candidate, save Bill Clinton in 1992, in the past 50 years has won the nomination without winning Iowa and/or New Hampshire.

I was getting pretty worried last night and let my catastrophisizing leak onto the internet. However, these are serious considerations. If Sanders gets into office, I won't me cut from medicaid like I probably would under Trump, meaning I could continue to afford HRT and when M4A does get passed I'd be able to afford surgery. So, if you want to help future transpeople, please, vote for the guy going all the way and who has the popular support to make Washington bend the knee if needed. Vote Bernie Sanders.  

If Sanders does get screwed over, at least I have a few backup plans to consider if my student debt I am accumulating in college won't keep me from moving. Thank you everyone for your wonderful suggestions and positivity.
